facts.text: A token is about four characters of English, or roughly three quarters of a word. That is a rule of thumb: code, numbers and many other languages use more tokens per word.
The KV cache for one 128k-token sequence on a 70B-class model with grouped-query attention is about 40 GiB in 16-bit precision, before you count the weights.
Training compute is roughly 6 × parameters × tokens FLOPs; a forward pass at inference is about 2 × parameters FLOPs per token.
Reciprocal rank fusion uses only ranks, not scores, so it merges keyword and vector results without calibrating them. The usual constant k = 60 comes from the 2009 paper that introduced it.
Decoding is usually memory-bandwidth-bound: every new token reads all the weights once, so batching more requests is how you buy throughput.
Simon Willison coined the term “prompt injection” in September 2022, by analogy with SQL injection.
Anthropic announced MCP in November 2024; the first specification version is dated 2024-11-05.
Since the 2026-07-28 specification, MCP is stateless: no initialize handshake, and every request carries its protocol version and client capabilities (verified Nov 2026).
FlashAttention computes exact attention without ever writing the full attention matrix to slow GPU memory. It is an IO trick, not an approximation.
pass@k rewards succeeding once in k tries; pass^k demands success every time, which is closer to what an agent’s users experience.
The Chinchilla paper (2022) found compute-optimal training uses roughly 20 tokens per parameter. Many modern models train on far more to make inference cheaper.
In “Lost in the Middle” (2023), models used facts at the start and end of a long context better than facts in the middle.
Binary quantization stores one bit per embedding dimension, 32 times smaller than float32. Systems usually rescore the top results with full-precision vectors.
LoRA with rank 16 on a 4096 × 4096 weight matrix trains 131,072 values instead of about 16.8 million.
Two labelers who each mark 90% of items positive agree about 82% of the time by pure chance. That is why Cohen’s kappa, not raw agreement, is the standard.
Rich Sutton’s 2019 essay “The Bitter Lesson” argues that general methods that scale with computation beat hand-built knowledge in the long run.
Speculative decoding, done with the standard acceptance rule, produces exactly the target model’s output distribution. The draft model changes only how fast you get there.
Prompt caching rewards append-only context: change one token early in the prompt and everything after it misses the cache.
The OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications lists prompt injection as risk number one (LLM01).
A2A 1.0.0 shipped on 12 March 2026 with breaking changes, and 1.0.1 followed on 26 May 2026 (verified Nov 2026).
Claude Code’s MCP tool search defers MCP tool definitions once they would exceed 10% of the context window (verified Nov 2026).
